# Vector-Raster Operations

## Loading

Using the `terra::rast()` function, we can load raster data from downloaded sources. Note that the most common format is .tif


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
r.nlights <- rast('../../NL')

inMemory(r.nightlights) #note: not loaded in memory!

plot(r.nlights)
```
:::


Multilayer format: NETCDF .nc

we will blow up the graph if we do not explicity select a sublayer


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
r.spei <- rast()

plot(r.spei[[1]]) # note the [[x]]
plot(r.spei[[10]])
plot(r.spei[[15]])
plot(r.spei[[21]])
```
:::


## Extraction

Extracting the raster value from each cell, where the vertices of a vector object is overlaying the cells. Here, we are using the `exactextractr::exact_extract()` function, as it is computationally efficient; if we want more precise raster values (at the cost of more computational power), we would use `exactextractr::extract()`

**Note**: requires standardization from sf vector into `SpatVec()`

Under the hood, it must extract vector type of data into spatvec() type of data
It transforms sf into spatvec() to turn into more coordinates

## Rasterization

Rasterizing sf vector data: transform a simple feature object into a raster object. Works by assigning non-missing values for the intersection raster grid cells (pixels); otherwise, leaves missing.

**Very computationally demanding**; only has one realist (but powerful) use case: distances over *friction surfaces*

Intuition: distances between two ports over the seine river;  

  * `rasterize()`, 
  * `transition()`, 
  * `shortestpath()`


::: {.cell}
